nodes_add.name: Shiv Baba (the Supreme Soul, as received by the Brahma Kumaris)
nodes_add.note: God as an incorporeal point of light who, members believe, spoke through Lekhraj from the 1930s and through Dadi Gulzar after 1969.

nodes_add.name: Om Radhe (Mamma)
nodes_add.note: Headed the trust committee of young women formed in October 1937; first administrative head of the Brahma Kumaris; died 24 June 1965. Cross-examined before a Hyderabad magistrate, January 1939.

nodes_add.name: Dadi Prakashmani
nodes_add.note: Born Rama, Hyderabad, Sindh, about 1922; joined Om Mandali at about fourteen in 1936; shared administration with Didi Manmohini after January 1969 and was chief administrative head until her death at Mount Abu on 25 August 2007.

nodes_add.name: Dadi Janki
nodes_add.note: Chief administrative head 2007 to her death on 27 March 2020 aged 104.

nodes_add.name: Nolini Kanta Gupta
nodes_add.note: Revolutionary companion of Sri Aurobindo and long-time general secretary of the Sri Aurobindo Ashram. Birth and death years from general knowledge; not re-checked in this batch.

nodes_update.name: Dada Lekhraj (Brahma Kumaris)
nodes_update.note: Lekhraj Khubchand Kripalani; born Hyderabad, Sindh, 1876 per the movement (1884 in the WRSP timeline); Om Mandali from the mid-1930s; trust of young women October 1937; Karachi c. 1938-1950; Mount Abu from 1950; died 18 January 1969.

nodes_update.name: Sri Chinmoy
nodes_update.note: Chinmoy Kumar Ghose, born Shakpura, Chittagong, 27 August 1931; Sri Aurobindo Ashram from 1944; New York 13 April 1964; UN peace meditations from 1970; died Jamaica, Queens, 11 October 2007.

edges_upsert.note: The movement's central claim: the Supreme Soul spoke through Lekhraj's body; the murlis are the record. Visions dated 1936 by the movement, 1931 by the WRSP timeline.
His satsang in Hyderabad from about 1934 read the Gita and chanted Om; raised a Vaishnava Hindu (INFORM).
Made head of the trust committee of eight young women, October 1937 (Brahma Kumaris, Our Journey).
Joined 1936; with Didi Manmohini took over administration after his death in January 1969; chief administrative head to 2007.
Succeeded her as chief administrative head in 2007.
Entered the Sri Aurobindo Ashram in 1944 aged twelve; stayed about twenty years; New York from April 1964. No formal initiation by Aurobindo recorded.
Grew up in the ashram under the Mother's direction, 1944-1964.
By Sri Chinmoy's own account he was Nolini Kanta Gupta's personal secretary for about eight years.

places.name: Hyderabad, Sindh
places.what: Birthplace; Om Mandali satsang from the mid-1930s; trust of young women formed October 1937

places.name: Clifton, Karachi
places.what: Community lived in rented houses on Victoria Road, Clifton, from about 1938-39 to 1950

places.name: Pandav Bhawan, Mount Abu
places.what: Headquarters from 1950; Lekhraj died here 18 January 1969 (coordinates reused from existing Mount Abu entry)

places.name: Jamaica, Queens, New York
places.what: Home and centre of his community; died here 11 October 2007

glossary.def: Krishna's flute. Among the Brahma Kumaris, the daily talks believed to be God speaking through Brahma Baba, read aloud each morning in every centre.
In Brahma Kumaris teaching, the short period between the end of the Iron Age and a new Golden Age, when God comes to teach. They say we are living in it now.
Unmanifest. The Brahma Kumaris use it for Brahma Baba after his death in 1969 and for the messages they believe he gave through Dadi Gulzar.
The Brahma Kumaris' term for being aware of oneself as a soul, a point of light, as opposed to body-consciousness, identifying with the body.
"Fountain-art." Sri Chinmoy's name for his paintings, begun in 1974.
Sri Chinmoy's ideal of going beyond one's own previous limits, in sport, art or meditation, competing only with oneself.
Indian English for a guru with a mass following, often used in the press with "self-styled", and frequently for figures facing criminal cases.
A camp or seat; in north India, the headquarters of a sect and its leader, as in the Dera Sacha Sauda of Sirsa.

issues: dada-lekhraj.mdx: birth year conflict (1876 in Brahma Kumaris and INFORM; 1884 and death 'at 85' in the WRSP timeline). Both given in the glance.
dada-lekhraj.mdx: date of the visions and founding conflict (1936 visions per the movement; 1931 visions in Benares and 1932 founding per WRSP/INFORM). Text gives both.

dada-lekhraj.mdx: whether the Sind government formally banned Om Mandali in 1939 is unresolved. Wikipedia (citing Coupland 1944 and Hardy 1984) says it was declared an unlawful association; WRSP says Premier Allah Bux told the assembly there was no legal basis; The Friday Times part IV reports only the demands. Text reports the conflict. Coupland and Hardy not seen directly.

dada-lekhraj.mdx: Karachi custody case (girls returned to their mothers, upheld on appeal) rests on Wikipedia's summary of Hodgkinson (2002); The Friday Times reports warrants and girls taken from Om Nivas. Check Hodgkinson before final.

dada-lekhraj.mdx: no explicit Brahma Kumaris statement on the post-1969 succession disputes or on the 1976 prediction was found; the organisation's own account of the Dadi Prakashmani era (shared leadership with Didi Manmohini, growth, UN status) is used, and its INFORM responses on families and child protection. The AIVV/PBK split is mentioned without its later legal cases (Virendra Dev Dixit), which were not researched.
dada-lekhraj.mdx: Babb (1986) listed in further reading without page-level checking.

sri-chinmoy.mdx: Salon (2014), San Diego CityBeat (2005), New York Post and The Joy of Sects (1994) allegations are cited via Wikipedia's summary; the original articles were not fetched. PIX11 (2016) and Village Voice (2007) were fetched. The 2004 lawyer's denial is via Wikipedia.
sri-chinmoy.mdx: Terry Todd's conclusion on the lifts is paraphrased from Wikipedia; the original Todd article was not seen. No Centre response to Todd was found.
sri-chinmoy.mdx: Nolini Kanta Gupta secretaryship is Sri Chinmoy's own claim (attributed). Node nolini-kanta-gupta born/died (1889/1983) not re-verified in this batch.
sri-chinmoy.mdx: 'Mount Everest of ultramarathons' (New York Times) seen only as quoted on Wikipedia; used without quotation marks.

new-revelations.mdx: the intro introduces Kalki Bhagavan, Nithyananda and Dhirendra Shastri in one sentence each from the unit notes and general reporting; re-check against their profiles when written.

new-revelations.mdx (godmen): Asaram's Gujarat appeal is described as pending in the Gujarat High Court per Telangana Today (Sept 2026); its listing date is unknown. He was on medical parole until 26 October 2026 and was reported returned to Jodhpur on 27-28 October 2026 with a case registered for late surrender; this is left out as transient. LiveLaw and The Week differ on whether the High Court kept the POCSO counts; the text avoids the point.

new-revelations.mdx (godmen): Ram Rahim's year of conviction in the Ranjit Singh case (2021) was not seen on a fetched page, so no year is given. The status of his appeal against the 2017 rape conviction in the High Court was not checked.

new-revelations.mdx (godmen): Rampal's second 2018 murder case (FIR 430, one death): whether its sentence is also suspended, and whether he has actually left jail after the April 2026 bail, could not be confirmed. Wikipedia lists him as out on bail since 9 April 2026; The Tribune dates the suspension 4 September 2025 (Wikipedia says August 2025), so the text says 2025.

new-revelations.mdx (godmen): Chandraswami: 'no charge followed' the Jain Commission naming and 'without a criminal conviction' rest on obituaries (Deccan Herald, The News Minute) that report no conviction; the final outcome of the ED penalty appeals after 2011 is unknown.
No godman figures were added to the graph, by design; author may want tree-free mentions only.
Places: Clifton (Karachi), Shakpura and Jamaica (Queens) coordinates are approximate; Mount Abu coordinates reuse the existing places.json entry, which may be a duplicate.

dada-lekhraj: Founded 1936 in Hyderabad, Sindh; Om Mandali; October 1937 trust committee of eight young women headed by Om Radhe; Karachi 1938-1950; Mount Abu 1950; 'attains ascension on January 18 1969'; Om Radhe died 24 June 1965; Prakashmani chief after 1969 to 2007; Janki 2007-2020; Hridaymohini to March 2021; Ratanmohini died 8 April 2025 aged 101; BK Mohini Didi current head; 19 centres 1959; over 5,750 branches in more than 130 countries; ECOSOC 1983 -> https://www.brahmakumaris.com/journey/

Born 1876 in Sindh; diamond merchant; visions 1936; committee of 'eight young women' 1937; Mount Abu 1950; passed 1969 -> https://ie.brahmakumaris.org/about-us/the-brahma-kumaris-story/brahma-baba-the-founder
About 400 members at move to Mount Abu 1950; Karachi about a year after formation -> https://ie.brahmakumaris.org/about-us/the-brahma-kumaris-story/humble-beginnings

Born 15 December 1876, Hyderabad; died 18 January 1969 Mount Abu; accused of sorcery; Karachi court 1939 girls returned to mothers, upheld; unlawful association under 1908 Act (Coupland); 'Is this Justice?' by Radhe; Mount Abu 5 May 1950; a relative reported Shiva spoke through him -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dada_Lekhraj

Born 1884; visions 1931 Benares; satsang 1934 reading Gita, chanting Om; 1937 trust; 1938 Anti-Om Mandli Committee; March 1939 Premier Allah Bux 'no legal basis' for ban; ~300 moved to Karachi 1939; died 1969 at 85; 1976 named as year of destruction in early documents; AIVV split late 1970s rejecting Dadi Gulzar -> https://wrldrels.org/?p=17230

Show-cause notice 17 Aug 1938 (CrPC 107/112); picketing; Om Radhe cross-examined 31 Jan 1939 on magic, hypnotism; kidnapping complaint inquired, no action; demands for ban under Criminal Law Amendment Act Feb 1939; Clifton, Victoria Road houses -> https://thefridaytimes.com/02-Jul-2021/time-travel-through-sindh-and-social-reform-in-the-1930s-iv

Lekhraj 1876-1969, gem trader, Vaishnavite; trust of female followers; Raja Yoga 'does not involve mantras or breathing techniques or special postures'; God a point of light; body consciousness and vices lust, anger, greed, ego; 5,000-year cycle, four ages, Confluence Age; souls repeat actions; Sakar and Avyakt murlis (Dadi Gulzar); celibacy, sattvic diet without onion/garlic, white dress; family complaints, wills 'undue influence on vulnerable members'; BK responses on bereavement visits and child protection since 2001; 'no allegations of widespread or systemic child abuse'; PBK split -> https://inform.ac/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/Brahma-Kumaris-2020-1.pdf

Quote 'Soul consciousness is the awareness that we are souls'; 'visualizing oneself as a point of light'; body consciousness definition -> https://www.brahmakumaris.com/blog/rajyog-meditation/understanding-soul-consciousness/
Quote 'daily teachings (Murli), spoken through Brahma'; God 'beyond birth and death'; 1936 revelation -> https://www.brahmakumaris.com/blog/brahma-baba-articles/recognizing-god-through-brahma-baba/
Quote 'A worldwide spiritual movement led by women'; 'personal transformation and world renewal through Rajyoga Meditation' -> https://www.brahmakumaris.com/about-us/

Dadi Prakashmani born Rama 1922 Hyderabad; joined Diwali 1936 at about 14; shared administration with Didi Manmohini after 18 Jan 1969; died 25 Aug 2007; 'leader who created other leaders' -> https://www.brahmakumaris.com/wisdom/blog/eng/dadi-prakashmani-lifestory-leadership-world-service
Dadi Prakashmani died 25 August 2007 Mount Abu; head 1969-2007 -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dadi_Prakashmani
Dadi Ratan Mohini died aged 101 in Ahmedabad hospital, April 2025 -> https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/india/brahma-kumaris-head-dadi-ratan-mohini-passes-away
sri-chinmoy: Born Shakpura, East Bengal, 27 August 1931; 20 years at the ashram; New York 1964; 120,000 poems, 13,000 Bengali and 7,000 English songs, over 140,000 artworks, nearly 1,600 works; quotes 'a harmonious lifestyle that blends the inner discipline of prayer and meditation with the dynamism of modern life' and 'meditation is everyone's birthright' -> https://us.srichinmoycentre.org/sri_chinmoy

Youngest of seven; father died 1943, mother months later; ashram 1944 aged 12; athletics, cottage industries; secretary to Nolini Kanta Gupta ~8 years (his claim); inner message to go west; UN meditations from 1970; painting from 1974 (Jharna-Kala); Soul-Birds Dec 1991; peace concerts from 1984 (Royal Albert Hall, Carnegie Hall); weightlifting from 1985 at 54 after knee injury; Peace Run April 1987, usually biennial; NYT 'Mount Everest of ultramarathons'; heart meditation, before 7 a.m.; vegetarian, no drugs/alcohol, celibacy; died 11 Oct 2007 Jamaica, Queens, heart attack, 76; Terry Todd on lifts; allegations (Joy of Sects 1994, CityBeat 2005, Salon 2014, NY Post); never sued or charged; lawyer denied 2004 allegations; Tamm memoir 2009, banished at 25; Santana -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sri_Chinmoy

Arrived JFK 13 April 1964 met by Sam Spanier and Eric Hughes; Indian Consulate June 1964 to resignation 13 June 1967; AUM Centre incorporated Puerto Rico 22 July 1966 and New York 12 August 1966 -> https://srichinmoylibrary.com/mcy-113e1
Quote 'we compete with ourselves, with our own achievements, not with others' -> https://www.srichinmoylibrary.com/ims-13
Self-transcendence; seed to banyan; progress credited to God's grace -> https://srichinmoylibrary.com/rs-19
